decisions.quote: In this article, Salomon's model and the research in which the model was tested are discussed, and a replication study is presented. The study determines the internal structure of the Dutch versions of Salomon's instruments and tests some predictions following from the model. Unlike their American peers, Dutch children do not unconditionally perceive television as an easy medium.
decisions.reason: No prior adjudication or state file exists for this work. The supplied primary source contains only the publisher landing-page abstract and reference list for Beentjes (1989). The abstract states that it presents a Dutch replication study determining the internal structure of Dutch versions of Salomon's instruments, testing predictions from Salomon's (1981) model, and comparing Dutch children's media perceptions to those of their American peers. However, the abstract does not cite which empirical study is replicated, and the reference list contains two distinct 1984 empirical articles on children's media perceptions and effort investment: Salomon (1984), 'Television is "easy" and print is "tough": The differential investment of mental effort in learning as a function of perceptions and attributions' (Journal of Educational Psychology, 74, 647-658), and Salomon & Leigh (1984), 'Predispositions about learning from print and television' (Journal of Communication, 34, 119-135), the latter of which is shipped row 1863 (DOI 10.1111/j.1460-2466.1984.tb02164.x). Without the article body, the evidence cannot resolve whether the retested target is already represented by shipped row 1863, is Salomon (1984), or includes both.
